Yes — that feels distinctly gentler, exactly as I'd hoped. Clicking "Archive bookmark" quietly moved it out of All bookmarks, told me it "moved to Archive," and the Archive count went up — and crucially there was none of that "this can't be undone, you'll lose your note" alarm that delete has. It even reassured me the bookmark and all its details are safe. So it reads as "tidying away," not "destroying," which is the whole distinction I wanted between the two.

And the placement is right. Having Archive sit above the permanent-delete area in the details puts the softer, everyday action first and keeps the scary one tucked at the very bottom, so I'm not likely to reach for delete when I only meant to set something aside. Its own spot in the sidebar makes sense too.

Two things I'll want to confirm to be sure it's the reversible "set aside" I asked for: that an archived bookmark really is kept out of my normal library *and* my everyday searches — it shouldn't clutter those up — but that I can go to that Archive view, see it with everything intact, and bring it back out when I want it. Can we check those next?
